title: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN: security flaw used in attacks
verdictReason: Attacks are confirmed. The vulnerability is 3 days old, so many systems are likely still unpatched. It affects a product that faces the internet or gives remote access.
rankWhy: Exploitation is confirmed by an authoritative source.
The product faces the internet or gives remote access.

category.label: VPN, firewall or gateway
category.why: It sits at the edge of your network and faces the internet, so attackers can reach it directly.
category.doThis: If you have it, patch it today. If you cannot, block access to it from the internet until you can.

summary: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN contains a use of single-factor authentication vulnerability that may allow a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls. Successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA).
fix: CISA's instruction: apply the vendor's fix, or stop using the product if no fix exists. CISA set Nov 20, 2026 as the deadline for US federal agencies. It is a US government deadline; use it as a guide.
